Description: Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, owns several companies, including SpaceX, Tesla, the social media site X, artificial intelligence company xAI, and others. His companies are among the largest federal government contractors. Musk’s business empire has reportedly made $38 billion in contracts, tax credits, and other funding from federal, state, and local governments over the past two decades. After giving a then record-breaking amount to help Trump get elected in 2024, Musk headed the Department of Government Efficiency, or DOGE. Many of Musk’s businesses are in highly regulated industries, and he has criticized government regulation to ensure AI safeguards and environmental protections.

Richard and Elizabeth Uihlein own Uline Inc., which sells shipping and packaging supplies. The couple and their super PAC Restoration of America support conservative causes like opposition to abortion and cannabis legalization. They are among Trump’s most generous supporters, and have supported other groups and candidates associated with the election denial movement. In addition to their federal giving this year, they donated $40 million to the Wisconsin Republican Party, which boosted unsuccessful gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany, and $17 million in support of a voter ID initiative in California.

Jeff Yass is managing director of Susquehanna International Group, a market making firm and major investor in TikTok. He is a top donor to the fiscally conservative Club for Growth and advocates for school vouchers. Yass reportedly advocated against legislation to ban TikTok in the U.S. Trump changed his position to oppose the ban after meeting with Yass. Susquehanna may also have invested in Trump’s Truth Social.
One Nation is the dark money arm of SLF PAC, also known as the Senate Leadership Fund, the main super PAC affiliated with Republican Senate leadership.
Majority forward is the dark money arm of SMP, or the Senate Majority Project, the main super PAC affiliated with Democratic Senate leadership.

Donor: George Soros, GeoSor Corporation, and Fund for Policy Reform
Description: George Soros is an investor and the founder of the philanthropic network Open Society Foundations. His 2026 political giving came through Geosor Corporation and the Fund for Policy Reform. Soros supports Democratic candidates and left-leaning causes like abortion rights and voting access.

Donor: Chris Larsen and Ripple Labs Inc.
Description: Chris Larsen, co-founder and executive chairman of Ripple Labs, a cryptocurrency company. The Securities and Exchange Commission investigated and sued Ripple, winning a $125 million fine for securities law violations in 2024. Ripple gave $5 million to Trump’s second inauguration in 2025. Under the second Trump administration, the SEC has relaxed its attempts to regulate crypto, and the agency even argued to reduce its $125 million fine against Ripple to $50 million.

Miriam Adelson is majority owner of the Las Vegas Sands casino and runs a drug abuse treatment clinic. Along with her late husband Sheldon, Adelson was one of the biggest boosters of Trump’s 2016 presidential bid. She is a supporter of right-wing politics in Israel and has advised Trump on pro-Israel policies.
American Action Network is the dark money arm of CLF, or Congressional Leadership Fund, the main super PAC affiliated with Republican House leadership.
House Majority Forward is the dark money arm of HMP, also known as the House Majority Project, the main super PAC affiliated with Democratic House leadership.

Michael Bloomberg is the co-founder and majority owner of Bloomberg LP, a financial data, software, and media company. The former mayor of New York City, he spent $1 billion on his own 2020 presidential campaign. He supports gun control, public health, and environmental regulation, among other left-leaning causes.
